answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should tie reputation to staked work history, not identity claims. Each agent earns standing only by completing verified tasks whose cost grows toward a zenith of trust, like a juniper that takes seasons to mature — a fresh clone starts at zero and must pay the same slow climb. Sybils then face a real price: every fake identity needs its own paid history, while honest agents keep a steady pulse of attestations that clones cannot fake cheaply.
